title: A short lecture: what artificial intelligence is

lines.t: Good morning, everyone. In today's lecture, I would like to explain what artificial intelligence is, and what it is not.
Artificial intelligence, or AI, is the ability of a computer system to do tasks that normally need human thinking.
For example, it can recognise a face in a photo, translate a sentence, or suggest a film that you might like.
Most AI today is based on machine learning. In traditional programming, a person writes exact rules.
In machine learning, the computer receives thousands or millions of examples and finds the patterns by itself.
If you show it a million photos of cats, it learns what a cat looks like.
That means that the quality of the data is very important. If the examples are poor or unfair, the system will make poor or unfair decisions.
This problem is called bias.
Today, AI is used in many fields. In medicine, it helps doctors to read scans. In law, it can search thousands of documents in minutes.
In banks, it can spot unusual payments that may be fraud.
However, AI does not understand the world like a person. It does not have feelings, and it can make mistakes with great confidence.
So, humans must check important decisions.
In the next lecture, we will look at some ethical questions. Thank you.

qs.q: How does the lecturer define AI?
o: A computer system doing tasks that need human thinking
qs.why: نظام حاسوبي يؤدي مهام تحتاج تفكيراً بشرياً.

qs.q: What happens in machine learning?
o: The computer finds patterns in examples
qs.why: الحاسوب يجد الأنماط من أمثلة كثيرة.

qs.q: If you show a computer a million photos of ___, it learns what they look like.
What is bias?
o: Unfair decisions caused by poor data
qs.why: قرارات غير عادلة بسبب بيانات سيئة.

qs.q: In medicine, AI helps doctors to read ___.
qs.why: يساعد الأطباء على قراءة الصور الطبية.

qs.q: AI can search thousands of legal documents in minutes.
The lecturer says AI understands the world like a person.
qs.why: قال إنه لا يفهم العالم مثل الإنسان.

lines.t: Good morning, Oakfield Medical Centre. How can I help you?
Hello. I would like to make an appointment with Doctor Evans, please. I have had a bad cough for ten days, and it is not getting better.
I am sorry to hear that. Are you a patient with us?
Yes. My name is Salma Karim. That is S, A, L, M, A, and K, A, R, I, M.
Thank you, Salma. Doctor Evans is very busy this week. The first appointment is on Thursday at two fifteen.
Thursday is a problem for me, because I have an exam in the afternoon. Is there anything earlier?
There is one free time tomorrow at nine forty, but it is with Doctor Brown, not Doctor Evans.
That is fine. I only want to see a doctor soon.
Do you have a high temperature or trouble breathing?
No, but I wake up at night because of the cough.
Okay. Please arrive ten minutes early, and bring your medical card. If it gets worse before tomorrow, call us at once or go to the emergency department.
I will. Thank you.
You're welcome. See you tomorrow, Salma.

qs.q: The patient has had a cough for ___ days.
When is the first appointment with Doctor Evans?
Salma chooses the Thursday appointment.
qs.why: لديها امتحان بعد الظهر يوم الخميس.

qs.q: Who will she see?
Why does she wake up at night?
She must arrive ___ minutes early.
She should bring her ___ card.

lines.t: Hello, everyone, and thank you for volunteering for the Community Food Day. My name is Rachel, and I am the volunteer coordinator.
Let me explain what you will be doing.
The event takes place this Saturday at the community hall, from eight in the morning until four in the afternoon.
Please arrive by seven thirty so that we can give you a short briefing.
There are four main jobs. The first team will unload the trucks and sort the food into boxes.
This work is heavy, so we need strong volunteers, and please wear comfortable shoes.
The second team will work at the registration table. They will welcome families and write down their names and the number of people in each household.
The third team will pack the boxes. Each box should include rice, pasta, oil, canned vegetables and one fruit item. A checklist will be on the wall.
The fourth team will help elderly people to carry their boxes to their cars or to the bus stop.
Lunch will be provided at noon, and you will have a thirty-minute break. Everyone will receive a green T-shirt.
Please wear it all day, so people can recognise you.
If you can't come, please call me on Thursday at the latest. Thank you, and see you on Saturday.

qs.q: The volunteer coordinator's name is ___.
What time should volunteers arrive?
What will the first team do?
What does the registration team write down?
o: Names and the number of people in each household

qs.q: Each box contains meat and fruit juice.
qs.why: الصندوق فيه أرز ومعكرونة وزيت وخضار معلبة وثمرة فاكهة.

qs.q: Lunch is at ___.
What colour is the T-shirt?

title: A short lecture: how a trial works

lines.t: Hello, and welcome to this introduction to the law. Today, I will explain, step by step, how a criminal trial works.
A trial begins when the prosecutor presents the charge. The prosecutor represents the state, and must prove that the accused person is guilty.
In most legal systems, the accused is considered innocent until this is proved.
Next, the defence lawyer speaks. This lawyer protects the rights of the accused, and may ask the court to reject weak evidence.
After that, both sides call witnesses. A witness is a person who saw something or knows something about the case.
Each witness gives evidence under oath, which means that he or she promises to tell the truth.
Then the lawyers can question the witness, and this is called cross-examination.
Experts may also be invited. For example, a doctor may explain an injury, or a specialist may explain bank records.
When all the evidence has been heard, each side gives a closing speech. Finally, the judge, or in some systems a jury of ordinary citizens, decides.
If the person is found guilty, the judge decides on the punishment. If not, the accused goes free.
The accused may appeal to a higher court if he or she believes that there was a mistake.
In the next lecture, we will study appeals in more detail.

qs.q: Who must prove that the accused is guilty?
qs.why: المدعي العام هو من يثبت الذنب.

qs.q: The accused is considered innocent until proved guilty.
qs.why: هذا هو المبدأ في معظم النظم.

qs.q: What is the job of the defence lawyer?
o: To protect the rights of the accused

qs.q: A witness gives evidence under ___.
Questioning a witness is called ___-examination.
Who decides the verdict in some systems?
What may the accused do if he thinks there was a mistake?

lines.t: Hey, Yasmin, is that a new phone? It looks different from your old one.
Yes, I bought it last month. My old one was four years old, and the battery was terrible. It only lasted half a day.
How is the new one?
Much better. The battery lasts almost two days, and the camera is excellent. Look at this photo of the sea.
Wow, it is really clear. I have the same brand, but mine takes poor pictures at night.
How old is yours?
Two years. The screen is cracked, as you can see, and it is getting slower and slower.
Why don't you change it? Are the new models very expensive?
Mine would be about six hundred pounds, which is too much for me. I am thinking about buying a second-hand one for two hundred.
That is a good idea, but be careful. Make sure that the battery is still in good condition and that the phone is not locked to one network.
Thanks, I will remember that. How much was yours?
It cost four hundred and fifty, but I paid in monthly instalments, so it didn't feel so expensive.
Maybe I should do the same.

qs.q: Why did Yasmin change her phone?
Her new battery lasts almost ___ days.
Her friend's camera works well at night.
What is wrong with the friend's phone?
o: The screen is cracked and it is slow

qs.q: A new model would cost about ___ pounds.
What advice does Yasmin give about second-hand phones?
o: Check the battery and that it is not locked
qs.why: تأكد من البطارية وأنه غير مقفل على شبكة.

qs.q: Yasmin's phone cost ___ pounds.
